label: original-phase runs of 2/n-like tokens (weak)
explanation: Sparse (~1% of steps), diffuse unit. 89% of mass is in the original-input phase, ~6% at <DEL>, almost none during copy; never fires at t=0. Rate rises late in long sequences (orig_idx 7-8, L=9) and at t=1-2. Strongest token preference is input 2 (9.8x lift, 40% of mass), then n, l, y, 1, k; it also prefers when the previous tokens come from the same set and when the sequence has many digits, i.e. it seems to build up over consecutive tokens from {2,n,1,y,k,l}. Top activations are input 2 at the final original position followed by <DEL>. No single predicate captures it: input==2 alone gives dev F1 0.22 (mass 0.40); the best predicate (2 or n preceded by a set token) gives dev F1 0.31, mass recall 0.35; broader set-count predicates reach mass 0.80 but precision under 0.1. Does not fire in the copy phase or on most letters.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=1: 2, 1, l, y; t=5: 2, n, y, l; t=6: 2, n, y, l) and the previous input (most: 2, n, 1, y, k, c; least: m, b, -, d); timing cues that raise it most: t=8, L=9 & t=13, L=4 & t=3.
